response.markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Positive-edge coverage is only 1.86–4.25%. Transition evidence therefore reaches few sampled training targets. (2) Deployment/training residual MAE is approximately 53–126% of mean absolute residual magnitude. This motivates testing graph alignment, but does not establish ranking harm. (3) Qualitative feedback questions broad historical associations. Histories alone cannot establish current intent, ownership, compatibility, or satisfied needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Sampled evaluation can reverse model comparisons [Dallmann et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045). The pinned evaluator must remain the selection criterion, with full-catalog observations reported separately. (2) Plausible explanations may misrepresent influential evidence [Walk the Talk?](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/b5ec50eb177908f21f78ed0d76ed525c-Abstract-Conference.html). Simulator narratives should generate hypotheses rather than preference labels. (3) Metamorphic testing checks recommendation implementations through controlled changes [RecPack Tests](https://recsys.acm.org/recsys23/session-18/). Known interventions can validate whether probes detect the intended mechanism.

**Framework and directions.** Separate three questions: does evidence cover candidates, does it change ranking, and does the resulting ranking improve validation?

| Direction | Existing measurement | Missing evidence | Proposed intervention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence availability | Edge coverage | Benefit outside supported targets | Support shrinkage |
| Ranking influence | Raw residual magnitude | Boundary crossings | Residual scale audit |
| Temporal relevance | Qualitative feedback | Dependence on older events | History dropout |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Residual scale calibration | 3/6/3 | Originality: combines deployment diagnostics with selection; scalar calibration is established. Potential: cheaply isolates branch utility; cannot repair missing edges. Difficulty: scoring change is small; export and diagnostic parity require care. |
| Distinct-user support shrinkage | 4/6/5 | Originality: connects reliability to residual strength; shrinkage is established. Potential: suppresses fragile associations; sparse coverage may erase benefits. Difficulty: compact scoring rule; support counting and fold alignment complicate implementation. |
| Training history dropout | 2/6/4 | Originality: tests dependence on isolated events; regularization is familiar. Potential: may improve robustness; can remove useful recent evidence. Difficulty: small training change; retraining consumes budget. |

**Selected idea: deployment-consistent residual scale calibration.** At 0% progress, prioritize a cheap falsifiable intervention. For the supplied transition-residual implementation, expose the exact deployed score as `s_base + alpha * residual`, preserving its existing gate inside `residual`. Compare preregistered alpha values `{0, 0.5, 1}` using one frozen checkpoint and identical pinned validation candidates. Select only by macro validation HR@10; report category changes and top-10 turnover. This experiment estimates inference-time branch utility, not the benefit of retraining without it.

Retain the diagnostic API, restore module modes, report missing measurements explicitly, and verify exported-predictor parity. Preserve all four routes, seeds, splits, environment paths, and budget accounting. If the actual starting SASRec has no residual branch, report this prerequisite as absent rather than fabricating one.

idea.description: Expose and calibrate the existing transition branch at deployment: score_alpha = base_score + alpha * gated_transition_residual. Evaluate the fixed values 0, 0.5, and 1 on the pinned validation benchmark using one frozen checkpoint. This is an inference intervention for the supplied residual-bearing implementation; an unmodified SASRec without that branch does not satisfy the prerequisite.
idea.motivation: Measured positive-edge coverage is low, and deployment/training residual discrepancies are large relative to residual magnitude. Neither observation establishes harm, because small score changes can matter near ranking boundaries. A controlled scale intervention directly tests whether the deployed branch changes candidate ordering and whether those changes improve macro validation HR@10, without interpreting qualitative feedback as observed preference labels.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the exact base score and existing gate; alpha multiplies the complete deployed residual, avoiding double gating. Do not infer a residual from complete-minus-raw diagnostic means: those aggregates are insufficient for candidate scoring. If score decomposition is unavailable, add an explicit architecture-specific scoring hook and test reconstruction at alpha=1 before evaluation. Use a single fixed trained checkpoint, with alpha candidates frozen before validation results. Compare identical inputs, exclusion masks, candidate sets, and deterministic tie handling. Select one global alpha by equal-weight macro validation HR@10, resolving ties in favor of alpha=1; record all comparisons and category results. Do not claim paired uncertainty unless the host exposes paired outcomes. Separately report descriptive full-catalog unseen-item lists for the twenty prescribed training users; these are not relevance measurements. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model, no_grad, bounded diagnostic batches, and restore every submodule's original training flag in finally. Return metrics and metric_definitions, with counts and null plus reasons for missing measurements. Keep compatibility methods functional and make their default scores match deployed alpha. Update the predictor writer and checkpoint metadata to load alpha and the exact trained architecture; verify scores and rankings against the training-side model. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; environment-controlled SASREC_EPOCHS default 200; and trial-local artifacts. Count training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Use no hidden tests, extra data, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata, or changes to the host evaluator. Treat validation selection as adaptive model selection, not independent evidence of generalization.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze alpha_grid = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]
train baseline once under the prescribed seeds and epoch environment
freeze checkpoint
require explicit decomposition into base_score and deployed_gated_residual
assert score(alpha=1) reconstructs the original deployed score
for alpha in alpha_grid:
    write trial-local predictor with checkpoint, architecture, and alpha
    assert predictor/model score and ranking parity on public training inputs
    obtain pinned host validation HR@10 for all four categories
    record macro HR@10, category results, and costs
select alpha maximizing macro HR@10; break ties toward alpha=1
export selected predictor and diagnostic configuration
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save every module's training flag
    try:
        set view.model to evaluation mode
        with no_grad:
            measure bounded pairwise margins and residual-induced ranking changes
            include counts, definitions, missingness, and interpretation limits
        return {metrics, metric_definitions}
    finally:
        restore every saved training flag

originality.positive: Connects observed residual coverage and train/deployment discrepancies to a controlled intervention on the exact deployed scoring branch.
originality.negative: Scalar branch ablation and calibration are established methods; this is primarily a disciplined experimental contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can cheaply establish whether further work on transition support, graph alignment, or residual training is justified.
future_potential.negative: A scalar cannot recover missing transition evidence, represent current intent, or establish full-catalog relevance.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional training when the deployed score already exposes its residual branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct decomposition, diagnostic compatibility, predictor export, and score parity need explicit implementation; the proposal is unavailable for a branch-free model.

related_work.title: Dallmann et al.: sampled evaluation of sequential recommendation
contributions: Reports disagreement between sampled-candidate and full-catalog model comparisons.
Motivates separating benchmark selection from descriptive full-catalog diagnostics.
limitations: Does not establish that residual calibration improves this benchmark.
Does not justify replacing the pinned evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: Walk the Talk? — ICLR 2025
contributions: Provides evidence that plausible explanations can misrepresent influential recommendation evidence.
Supports testing model influence directly rather than treating narrative plausibility as causal evidence.
limitations: Does not supply current-intent or compatibility labels for the available users.
Does not validate the proposed residual scale selection rule.

related_work.title: A Framework and Toolkit for Testing the Correctness of Recommendation Algorithms — RecPack Tests
contributions: Applies metamorphic and property-based testing to recommendation implementations.
Motivates score reconstruction, branch-disable checks, and predictor parity verification.
limitations: Implementation correctness does not establish recommendation quality.
The supplied conference-session link is not evidence that this specific diagnostic protocol has been validated.
